install_tell: no standalone listener — Helix runs as an in-process controller/participant agent inside Pinot/other Helix-based systems, using an existing ZooKeeper ensemble (often the SAME ensemble tracked under the 'zookeeper' tome entry) as its only external-facing store
misconfig_patterns: Has NO distinct network port or listener of its own -- not directly Shodan-dorkable as a service
Detected only by connecting to a ZooKeeper ensemble already reachable (via 'zookeeper' 4lw/znode access) and walking the znode tree for Helix-specific paths

Hard fingerprint: znode root named after the cluster (e.g. /PinotCluster, /<clustername>) containing child znodes CONFIGS/, IDEALSTATES/, EXTERNALVIEW/, LIVEINSTANCES/, INSTANCES/, PROPERTYSTORE/, CONTROLLER/ -- this exact child-node set is what Helix (not raw application ZK usage) creates

Because it rides on ZK, every ZooKeeper misconfig in the 'zookeeper' tome entry (open 4lw wchs/dump, no ACL on znodes) applies transitively to Helix-managed clusters -- Helix adds no additional auth layer of its own

active_probe.false_positive_check: not a passive-dorkable fingerprint -- requires an already-reachable ZK ensemble (from the 'zookeeper' harvest) plus an active znode ls (e.g. via zkCli 'ls /') that surfaces the Helix-specific child-node set; do not run this as an independent Shodan dork, log it as 'detected via ZK znode structure, not a separate listener' per dispatch scope

deployment_tells: No independent banner -- inherits the ZooKeeper ensemble's exposure entirely
Presence confirmed only post-hoc, during ZK znode enumeration on hosts already flagged by the zookeeper dork set

Most commonly riding on ZK ensembles that also serve Kafka/Pinot -- cross-reference znode roots against known Helix-based products (Pinot, formerly Espresso/Gobblin at LinkedIn) rather than treating as a standalone population
pivot_paths: znode /CONTROLLER -> current controller leader identity -> pivots to the Pinot (or other Helix-based) controller host
znode /EXTERNALVIEW -> per-partition state map -> full data-node topology of the managed cluster
znode /PROPERTYSTORE -> cluster + resource configs, sometimes including connection info for downstream stores
